gaps.gap: rotateVaultKey calls sdk-vault POST /api/vault/keys/:key_id/rotate with a date-stamped idempotency key so a re-run in the same day cannot double-rotate, and the no-downtime property is REAL but it belongs to sdk-vault, not to this code: the SDK re-wraps under the new key while the previous one can still decrypt, exactly as the JWKS rotation in platform/auth keeps the outgoing key serving requests already in flight. LeadFlow cannot demonstrate that without a live vault. What is missing locally is a test proving a value encrypted before a rotation still decrypts after it, which needs a real key lifecycle - a stub would only assert that a stub was called. Also unbuilt: sdk-api-keys issuance, rotation and revoke for partner and extension access, which the task names alongside vault rotation and which nothing in LeadFlow calls.

gaps.criterion: Credential registry screen never renders a secret value
gaps.gap: The DATA the screen would render is provably safe: providerRegistryView returns a boolean configured flag rather than a masked string, and a test sets a real-looking ref then asserts the serialised view does not contain it. The masking decision is deliberate - sk_live_****4821 still leaks the prefix and the last four, enough to confirm a guess and reveal the product tier. But there is NO SCREEN: no component, no route, and no health or last-rotation display, all of which the task asks for. So the criterion is satisfied in the only place it can currently be violated and unproven where a person would actually see it. Closing it needs the registry screen, wired to this view function, plus a Gherkin step asserting no secret-shaped string appears in the rendered page.
